title: Redis Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Redis course.

entries.name: Store a value under a key
entries.summary: A key is a name used to find a value. SET stores a string, and GET reads that string back.

entries.name: Count with an atomic increment
entries.summary: INCR adds one to a key holding an integer.

example.code:
SET cma:books 0
INCR cma:books
INCR cma:books
GET cma:books

entries.name: Give a key an expiry
entries.summary: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit.

example.code:
SET cma:tip "Water the plants" EX 30
TTL cma:tip

entries.name: Check whether a key exists
entries.summary: EXISTS checks for a key without reading its value.

example.code:
SET cma:temporary "sample"
EXISTS cma:temporary
DEL cma:temporary
EXISTS cma:temporary

entries.name: Group fields in a hash
entries.summary: A hash stores several named fields under one Redis key.

example.code:
HSET cma:book:1 title "Moon Trip" pages 60
HGET cma:book:1 title

entries.name: Use a list as a small queue
entries.summary: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour.

example.code:
DEL cma:queue
RPUSH cma:queue "Moon Trip" "Garden Days"
LPOP cma:queue

entries.name: Keep each member once
entries.summary: A set holds unique members without a promised order.

example.code:
DEL cma:readers
SADD cma:readers Mia Sam Mia
SCARD cma:readers

entries.name: Rank values with a sorted set
entries.summary: A sorted set pairs each member with a score.

example.code:
DEL cma:scores
ZADD cma:scores 5 Mia 8 Sam 3 Ravi
ZRANGE cma:scores 0 -1 WITHSCORES

entries.name: Scan keys in small batches
entries.summary: SCAN walks through key names using a cursor.

entries.name: Group commands with MULTI
entries.summary: MULTI queues commands for EXEC. Redis runs that queued group without another client's commands between them.

example.code:
MULTI
SET cma:points 2
INCR cma:points
EXEC

entries.name: Publish a live message
entries.summary: Publish/subscribe sends live messages to clients currently listening to a channel.

example.code:
# Terminal A:
SUBSCRIBE cma:club-news
# Terminal B:
PUBLISH cma:club-news "Meeting at four"

entries.name: Choose what must survive a restart
entries.summary: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk.

example.code:
Example decision:
Cached book summary: can be loaded again if lost.
Only copy of a payment record: must not depend on an unreviewed cache setup.
Check the server's RDB snapshot and AOF settings, then test a practice restart.
